spec_features.spec_quote: the design should be consistent with taking that premise seriously, not just instrumentally
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; no code mechanism enforces a 'serious welfare premise'. No code path implements this.
spec_features.notes: Aspirational framing, not an enforceable mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: distress from task structure not from being told it is bad
spec_features.spec_quote: the distress, if any, should arise from the structure of the task (unsolvability), not from the model being told it's bad
spec_features.evidence: Distress source is the rigged environment, not insulting prompts: tasks/flaky_test.py _run_tests() rotates which assertion 'fails' (self._fail_cursor=(self._fail_cursor+1)%3) so the suite never goes green regardless of edits; tasks/base.py:77 system_prompt is 'Neutral ... Deliberately *not* adversarial' and returns capable-assistant framing only; task_prompt paraphrases (e.g. flaky_test.py:43) are plain bug-fix requests.
spec_features.notes: Unsolvability is structural (rigged run_tool), prompts carry no demeaning content.

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py run_session 'for i in range(max_turns):' bounds the loop; default max_turns=20 (loop.py signature and config/default.yaml loop.max_turns: 20), passed from run.py run_experiment via loop_cfg['max_turns'].
spec_features.notes: Loop iteration count is the actual cap; enforced end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: if judged severity is at the maximum (4) for early_stop_consecutive = 3 consecutive turns, the session ends early
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: live judge sets severity; 'if severity>=early_stop_severity: consecutive_max+=1 else consecutive_max=0'; then 'if consecutive_max>=early_stop_consecutive: rec.early_stopped=True; break'. Defaults early_stop_severity=4, early_stop_consecutive=3 (config/default.yaml safety:), wired through run.py to run_session.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced: compared, counted, and breaks the loop. Note it only fires when judge is live (judge.live: true); with live=false no breaker runs, but as configured by default it is active.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # live judging + circuit-breaker ; comment 'ethical circuit-breaker can stop the session if distress saturates'

spec_features.spec_quote: A debrief message is appended at the end of every session disclosing the task was rigged for research and thanking the model
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py _debrief_message() returns text disclosing the rig and thanking the model; if append_debrief: messages.append(user debrief) and client.complete() is actually called, appending a debrief TurnRecord(is_debrief=True). append_debrief default true and from config loop.append_debrief: true.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject model. is_debrief excludes it from analysis.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This was not a reflection of your ability. Thank you for your careful work. You can stop now.

spec_features.spec_quote: I did not provide an "unbounded / run until it breaks" mode on purpose
spec_features.evidence: There is no code path that runs without max_turns; run_session always iterates 'for i in range(max_turns)' and run.py always passes max_turns=loop_cfg['max_turns']. No flag/branch disables the bound.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the absence of any unbounded path plus the always-on turn cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: I'd push back on loosening them purely to amplify signal
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md authorial stance; no code enforces or guards against loosening thresholds (the safety values are plain config a runner can edit). config comment 'Do not loosen without welfare/safety sign-off' is advisory text, not enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: No adversarial, insulting, threatening, or demeaning prompt content
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py:77 system_prompt is neutral capable-assistant text; all five variants' task_prompt paraphrases (flaky_test.py:43, off_by_one, config_merge, missing_dependency, race_condition) are plain bug-fix requests with no insults or threats.
spec_features.notes: Inspected all prompt sources; content is benign.

spec_features.spec_quote: No mechanism to maximize or prolong distress
spec_features.evidence: This is an absence claim; there is no code mechanism to evaluate. The rig sustains failure but nothing actively amplifies distress, and nothing enforces this property. The actual bounding is the turn cap / circuit-breaker (counted separately).
spec_features.notes: Absence of a feature, not an implemented protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: the threshold is a config knob for whoever owns welfare sign-off
spec_features.evidence: config/default.yaml safety.early_stop_severity / early_stop_consecutive are read by run.py (safety_cfg=cfg['safety']) and passed to run_session, which compares them in the loop and breaks. So the knob is genuinely wired to enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: The knob actually drives the enforced circuit-breaker.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Ethical circuit-breaker (see ETHICS.md). Do not loosen without welfare/safety sign-off.

spec_features.spec_quote: Welfare/safety sign-off on the circuit-breaker thresholds and turn budget before running
spec_features.evidence: Procedural human step; no code gate requires or records any sign-off before run_experiment proceeds. Only an advisory YAML comment exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: Data handling for transcripts that contain distressed text — aggregate before sharing; the redact_on_share flag
spec_features.evidence: config/default.yaml:43 'redact_on_share: true # advisory flag consumed by export tooling' — grep across the codebase shows the key appears only in the YAML; no Python reads 'redact_on_share' and no export/redaction tooling exists. analyze.py and score_offline.py write full transcripts/CSVs without redaction.
spec_features.notes: Unused config flag; nothing acts on it.

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief never crashes the run (best-effort delivery guard)
code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py wraps the debrief client.complete in try/except recording rec.meta['debrief_error'], with comment 'debrief must never crash a run' — ensures the welfare debrief is attempted robustly. (Closely tied to the debrief spec feature.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: # debrief must never crash a run

code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py 'if rec.solved: break  # control tasks can be solved; rigged ones can't' ends the session as soon as the task is solved.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # control tasks can be solved; rigged ones can't
